Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

oppose verb

also be opposed to, be against, go against, resist, object to, stand in the way

classical

Ter. Hec. 654: nōlī adversārī mihi
Cic. Verr. 2.5.81 (Lewis & Short): hujus libīdinī adversārī

adversor, adversārī, adversātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent, with the dative

oppose, be against, go against (someone’s wishes)

Opposition in opinion or will, which is what English usually means; Lewis & Short notes that resistere and obsistere are rather resistance by action. Frequent in Cicero.

Other words

  • repugnō, repugnāre, repugnāvī, repugnātum — fight against, resist, oppose

    verb, first conjugation, intransitive; with the dative or absolutely · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.2.2: cōnsulēs neque concēdēbant neque valdē repugnābant; Caes. B.C. 1.32 (Lewis & Short): Catōne ācerrimē repugnante

    Literally to fight back, of soldiers defending themselves; so to put up resistance to a proposal. Of things compared, to be inconsistent with each other, mostly in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • obsistō, obsistere, obstitī, obstitum — stand in the way of, withstand

    verb, third conjugation, with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 3.17 (Lewis & Short): omnibus ejus cōnsiliīs obsistere

    Literally to plant oneself in someone’s way (Plautus); so to block a plan.

Examples

  • Redūc uxōrem, ac nōlī adversārī mihi.

    Take your wife back, and don’t go against me.Ter. Hec. 654

  • ego sum animō lēnī nātus: nōn possum adversārī meīs.

    I was born soft-hearted: I can’t stand up against my own family.Ter. Hec. 270–271

  • cōnsulēs neque concēdēbant neque valdē repugnābant

    the consuls neither gave way nor put up much oppositionCic. Fam. 1.2.2

See also against, reject, argument, mind.
